# Mixed initiative

## When to use

Use when an agent could either interrupt for direction or make a provisional decision: a vague design request, an ambiguous critique, a delegated exploration, or a high-cost action. This is a decision framework, not a visual reference.

## What to inspect

Read principles 5–11 together: dialogue, direct invocation/termination, costly guesses, precision under uncertainty, refinement and interaction history. The LookOut example supplies context for what those principles meant; the numbered list alone can sound more universal than the paper establishes.

## What to borrow and adapt

Identify the choice whose answer could change the result, whether the person can answer it, and the consequence of guessing. Ask about that choice while continuing independent work. Preserve settled answers and let the person reject, narrow or terminate a proposal.

For example, a community site may need a question about first-event confidence before a global direction is chosen. A person explicitly delegating typography has already answered who should make that choice. Treat those situations differently.

## Mismatches and limits

The paper presents principles and a historical scheduling prototype; it does not prove an optimal number of questions or a modern agent interview policy. It also does not imply that software should guess irreversible product facts, or that every uncertain implementation detail belongs to the person. Adapt the interruption/recovery tradeoff to the actual task and available controls.

# Adapt layout to script, direction and content

## When to use

Use when a direction relies on uppercase labels, tight tracking, manual line breaks, fixed Latin-width columns or hardcoded left/right positioning and must work in another script.

## What to inspect

Read base direction separately from language tagging, and distinguish structural layout from inline bidirectional content. In the Hangul document, inspect the draft status before using its font metrics, breaking or punctuation discussions.

## What to borrow and adapt

Preserve intended relationships and prominence while letting actual strings shape the layout. Use semantic direction and logical positioning where appropriate. Test mixed identifiers, numbers, punctuation, fallback fonts, long labels and localized errors.

A comparison card may retain its hierarchy while changing wrapping and alignment. Matching the English screenshot's line count is less important than readable grouping and correct order.

## Mismatches and limits

The Hangul publication is a Group Note Draft, not an endorsed Recommendation, and some sections remain unfinished. Language and direction are different properties; a blanket mirrored screenshot can mishandle icons, numbers or mixed text. These sources do not replace native-reader review or establish a single typographic style for all speakers of a language.

# Semantics are promises about behavior

## When to use

Use when a design introduces a custom button, menu, tab or other widget, or when a code rubric demands attributes and keyboard handlers without examining the actual element.

## What to inspect

Read the APG Introduction's scope and variation cautions before copying a pattern, then Read Me First and the relevant control's keyboard, name, role and state model. The button pattern also distinguishes a stable-label toggle from a label-changing command.

## What to borrow and adapt

Start with semantics appropriate to the operation. A native button already supplies behaviors that a styled generic element does not. If a custom role is necessary, implement and verify its promised interactions and focus management. Choose an accessible name from content or an appropriate relationship rather than requiring one attribute everywhere.

For a Save action, decide whether it is a stateful toggle or an action whose label changes. Preserve that model consistently for visual and assistive-technology users.

## Mismatches and limits

ARIA changes exposed semantics; it does not automatically add keyboard behavior or styling. Adding a role or label can also override useful native information. APG is informative, has no conformance model, and is not a comprehensive design system or production-ready component library. Its examples illustrate choices; variation still needs consistency with relevant specifications, practices and established keyboard conventions. APG notes mobile/touch and compatibility limits, so example code is not blanket production acceptance or a standalone conformance audit.

# Navigation: scent, depth and learned location

## When to use

Use when deciding between broad menus and deeper hierarchy, changing the location of frequent actions, or reorganizing a large reference catalog.

## What to inspect

Read the hierarchy experiment's category construction and results, then the menu model's treatment of visual search, pointing and learning. The former used a bounded encyclopedia retrieval task; the latter's calibration population was narrow. Keep the study contexts attached to their claims.

## What to borrow and adapt

Treat navigation as finding something under particular knowledge and frequency conditions. Compare known-item retrieval with exploratory browsing. Inspect whether labels provide useful clues, whether grouping matches the task, and whether repeated use benefits from stable locations.

For an expert issue tracker, keeping a learned action location may matter more than moving the most-used command to the first position. A newcomer may instead need explicit categories and examples.

## Mismatches and limits

Neither source yields a universal menu length or maximum depth. Faster performance on an artificial hierarchy does not establish the best structure for a content-rich mobile product. Adding levels to fit a remembered “seven items” slogan can increase work. Changing everything to a flat menu can also remove useful grouping. Source access is currently partial; reopen the menu model before using its exact constants.

# Use grouping to communicate relationships

## When to use

Use when a screen's relationships are ambiguous: labels seem attached to the wrong controls, repeated cards split one argument, or unrelated actions look like a single unit.

## What to inspect

Read the grouping argument and its commentary together. Distinguish the demonstrated cue interactions from the proposed ordering of perceptual processes. Inspect the original diagrams when using a particular visual demonstration; this card does not stand in for viewing those figures.

## What to borrow and adapt

Choose spacing, alignment, shared surfaces, borders and continuity to communicate the actual content relationships. Ask what people perceive as a group and which control belongs to which object. Use multiple consistent cues when one cue alone is ambiguous.

For a booking form, a shared boundary can bind a workshop's price, schedule and selection control. A boundary around every short sentence may instead imply separate objects that the content does not contain.

## Mismatches and limits

The sources do not prescribe an eight-pixel grid, require cards, or prove a particular CSS layout improves a product task. Competing cues and context can change the grouping. Peterson challenges a theory's serial interpretation, not every practical observation. Verify the intended relationship with the actual content and users rather than calling a decorative pattern scientifically mandatory.

# Discover preferences through critique and suggestions

## When to use

Use when the person's first criteria produce repetitive matches, when they say “I will know it when I see it,” or when rejecting a reference reveals a preference not present in the brief.

## What to inspect

Read how the paper distinguishes currently best matches from suggestions intended to reveal hidden preferences. Inspect the finite option model and user-study setup before borrowing its outcome claims.

## What to borrow and adapt

Include a plausible neighboring option that tests an assumption, not only several near-duplicates of the current favorite. Ask which property makes an example closer or wrong. Update the search profile from that reaction and make the changed criterion visible.

A person may reject an illustrated reference because it feels childish, while still wanting warmth. Search for human voice, material or local photography rather than treating the rejection as a request for corporate minimalism.

## Mismatches and limits

The study's preferred-item accuracy belongs to a finite apartment catalog. It does not establish a percentage benefit for creative design. Suggestions influence preferences as well as reveal them; do not present a leading decoy as neutral measurement. A single selection is not a permanent complete preference model, and the person may delegate an axis rather than choose it.

# Typography: distinguish preference, metrics and reading performance

## When to use

Use when selecting typography for sustained reading, interpreting a readability claim, or deciding whether a brand font conflicts with the actual reading task.

## What to inspect

In Legge/Bigelow, distinguish nominal type size, glyph metrics and visual angle. In Wallace, inspect font assignment, size normalization, exclusions, remote measurement and the within-reader comparison. The catalog preserves a prior inspected historical study, not a fresh prospective personalization test.

## What to borrow and adapt

Assess actual text at intended rendering sizes, scripts, devices and viewing conditions. Separate preference from reading effectiveness and from interface hierarchy. Preserve user adaptation and investigate a real problem before imposing personalization controls.

For a long-form club, test representative passages and long titles, then consider navigation and save controls separately. A font that suits a brand heading need not be the same role as reading text.

## Mismatches and limits

Do not promise the paper's observed fastest-versus-slowest difference as a deployable speed gain. The main study did not sample every font for every reader, excluded reading disabilities and did not find one universally fastest font. It does not require an app font picker or establish that serif/sans, novelty or one CSS size causes success. Original endpoints need access verification before quoting exact measurements.

# Plan usability samples around risk and variation

## When to use

Use when a team proposes a fixed participant count, has several user groups, or wants to interpret what a small formative round actually established.

## What to inspect

Read Nielsen's iteration and group qualifications, not only the title. In Faulkner, inspect the finite observed problem set, experience groups and resampling method. Those are different forms of evidence: cost-benefit guidance and variability demonstrated within one study.

## What to borrow and adapt

Select realistic tasks and relevant participants, record critical failures and what remains untested, and use findings to revise before another round. Coverage should include consequential variation in experience, device, language, accessibility needs or permissions when it changes the journey.

For a shared-tablet pickup tool, a small round with trained coordinators cannot establish that first-time substitutes can recover from an exception. Add the missing context deliberately rather than treating total headcount as sufficient.

## Mismatches and limits

The resampled percentages describe one application's known problems; they are not a guarantee for the next product. Do not replace a universal five-user rule with a universal larger number. Formative discovery, statistical comparison, rare-error estimation and accessibility evaluation have different sampling needs. No participant count by itself proves complete usability.

# Android adaptive Compose: layouts across form factors

## When to use

Choose this for an existing Compose application that needs coherent phone, tablet, foldable or desktop behavior. Its strongest design question is which content and controls belong together as available space, posture and input change; wider screens should not merely stretch the phone view.

## What to inspect

Read prerequisites first: the workflow expects Compose throughout and Navigation 3. Then inspect the relevant pane, state, desktop-input or tabletop reference. The pinned entrypoint includes experimental Grid, FlexBox and MediaQuery guidance; verify the precise dependencies and supported versions before adopting examples. The tabletop reference distinguishes rearranging identical content from layouts requiring different controls.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the inventory of list/detail relationships, the preservation of input, selection, navigation, scroll and playback state, and the demand to inspect multiple form factors. Ask which content benefits from simultaneous viewing and whether keyboard or pointer use changes the interaction. Follow actual hinge geometry and local coordinates when controls need to avoid a fold.

## Mismatches and limits

The source contains strong migration prescriptions, experimental API adoption and screenshot-test setup. Those are project decisions, not automatic consequences of choosing this reference. It also contains conflicting baseline directions: an earlier step records new references while the final step says not to update references before user review. Preserve diffs for review and resolve that conflict explicitly. No Android build, screenshot test, device interaction or generated layout was verified here.

## Related resource roles

- [pattern-material-navigation-bar](pattern-material-navigation-bar.md): For a bottom-navigation decision, compare the documented platform pattern while checking adaptive API and SDK compatibility separately.

# Anthropic frontend-design: subject-grounded visual direction

## When to use

Select this as a visual-direction procedure when the brief leaves meaningful creative freedom and the agent's first idea feels interchangeable. It is particularly relevant to subject-rich editorial, cultural, creative or marketing work. It can also sharpen an existing product direction without changing its functional priorities.

## What to inspect

Read the subject-grounding section, then the plan/review/build sequence and restraint section. Inspect the copy guidance when interface vocabulary or failure text contributes to the problem. The inspected file is a specific revision; check upstream changes before relying on its evolving list of generated-design tells.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the connection from product world to actual decisions: materials, audience, vocabulary and content should explain type, composition and motion. Its compact token/layout plan can make alternatives discussable before implementation. Ask the human about missing intent; preserve supplied brand choices and real content. Use the self-critique to challenge an arbitrary default, not to declare an unmeasured originality score.

For a repair workshop, the useful transfer is reasoning from tools, repair marks and customer confidence, rather than importing another brand's palette.

## Mismatches and limits

The author adopts a studio persona and advocates aesthetic risk and a memorable element. These are creative strategies, not universal requirements for operational tools or minor fixes. Current-look warnings are mutable taste heuristics; the file itself allows brief-specific exceptions. It supplies neither a complete flow methodology nor proof of accessible or usable results. Source inspection is not evidence that a generated interface looks good.

# Baseline UI: opinionated cleanup checklist

## When to use

Select this for a fast, scoped cleanup of an existing web surface when the project already resembles the supported component and Tailwind ecosystem. It can supply concrete review leads when “make it polished” has not yet been translated into inspectable defects.

## What to inspect

Read the target-file review contract and the exact category relevant to the issue. Inspect existing primitives before adopting the stack section. The checklist combines semantic/behavioral concerns with conventions about gradients, tracking, timing, shadows and accent usage.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the requirement to identify the offending snippet, explain the user consequence and suggest a code-level fix. Preserve the project’s components and test actual focus/error/empty behavior. For a crowded settings panel, use the hierarchy and local-error prompts to investigate legibility and recovery, then select only repairs justified by that panel.

## Mismatches and limits

The mandatory library choices and broad aesthetic prohibitions are house policy. They conflict with other legitimate visual directions, including intentionally expressive briefs. Fixed timing or blanket attribute recipes need contextual and standards checks. A clean checklist does not demonstrate usable behavior or absence of generic design. No cleanup was executed or visual result judged in this curation.

# Create DESIGN.md from observed governing evidence

## When to use

Select this when the task is to preserve an existing product’s design language in a document that other agents can use. It is particularly relevant when repeated local styling risks being mistaken for intentional shared design decisions.

## What to inspect

Read repository versus URL mode, evidence promotion, output schema and validation/export requirements. Repository mode traces governing tokens and owners. URL mode requires rendered and computed evidence and labels the result reconstructed; a screenshot cannot supply exact token names or hidden rationale.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the discipline of recording source, role, scope, recurrence and uncertainty before promoting a design rule. In an existing application, distinguish a shared semantic token from a one-off literal. Preserve accepted design choices and expose conflicts separately. The product owner can then correct a grounded interpretation instead of reviewing an invented brand manifesto.

## Mismatches and limits

The particular DESIGN.md schema and Google export commands are dependencies of this workflow, not universal documentation requirements. Its instruction to install/run current tooling is not authorized by catalog selection. # Fixing accessibility: targeted interface repair

## When to use

Select this when an implemented control, form, dialog or navigation element needs accessibility repair while preserving the surrounding design. Its bounded focus is more useful than re-running a broad aesthetic workflow for an unlabeled button or lost-focus problem.

## What to inspect

Read the relevant names, keyboard, focus, semantics or forms category and its tool-boundary section. Follow complex-widget questions into the applicable platform pattern or normative requirement. Priorities in this skill are a working review order, not conformance levels.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the connection from a concrete failure to a minimal change: native control where possible, correct name/state, associated error information, and intelligible focus movement. For a failed signup, inspect whether the error identifies a fix, whether the field retains input, and whether the recovery is operable without a pointer.

## Mismatches and limits

Prescriptive language such as every interaction being reachable by Tab needs widget-specific interpretation; composite widgets may use a tab stop plus arrow navigation. Attribute presence alone does not establish accessible naming or announcements. Do not add redundant ARIA where native semantics already provide the contract. No screen reader, browser or audit was run here, so this is a source-inspected repair procedure rather than accessibility acceptance.

# Fixing motion performance

## When to use

Select this when a specific transition or scroll-linked effect is visibly expensive or technically suspect. It fits a constrained performance repair after the purpose of the motion is understood; it is not a reason to animate an otherwise settled interface.

## What to inspect

Read the rendering glossary, mechanism choice and measurement sections together. Inspect the actual animated surface, frequency and interruption requirements. The layer section explicitly says not to assume compositor promotion; verify the relevant behavior with suitable tools when performance matters.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow batching of measurements/writes, bounded execution, off-screen stopping and cheaper alternative mechanisms. Preserve the interaction’s meaning while reducing unnecessary work. A small local affordance and a continuously changing full-screen surface need different cost analysis. Trace the existing library before changing its API or mixing another system into the same component.

## Mismatches and limits

Timing, blur limits and View Transition restrictions are opinionated guidelines rather than universal browser guarantees. Transforming an element can change layout semantics or hit targets even if it is cheap to composite. Choose techniques against measured behavior and current browser support. No animation, trace or benchmark was executed for this card; the evidence establishes the procedure’s contents only.

# Impeccable: surface modes and focused design commands

## When to use

Select this when the task needs a design procedure matched to the surface’s job: persuading, operating, reading or experiencing. Its focused commands can help distinguish a UX plan, a technical audit, a copy repair and a visual replacement instead of treating every request as a new landing page.

## What to inspect

Read Modes and routing, then only the applicable command reference. The shape reference is a planning-only interview and brief workflow. The canonical source template is skill/SKILL.src.md at this revision; the README identifies craft as a deprecated alias. Registry descriptions can lag.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the separation of surface purpose from the overall product category and the distinction between preserving refinement and replacing a visual world. Use the actual brief and existing interface as authority. For a developer tool, its marketing page, working editor and documentation can need different treatments while sharing identity.

## Mismatches and limits

The suite includes launcher binaries, optional downloads, hooks and project artifact writes. Its README says a new design fetches directions from the hosted catalog even with telemetry disabled; optional anonymous telemetry records directions shown and selected. It also says Claude Code hooks can run outside model approval and download the engine. These are source-described effects, not independently audited behavior; none were executed, and selection does not authorize them. Its command workflow and craft bans require deliberate adoption, not automatic precedence over user constraints. A command score is heuristic, not evidence of usability. No produced UI or efficacy comparison was inspected.

Select this as a planning-method reference when the user requests requirements exploration or a design document. It helps an agent examine an unfamiliar project and expose decisions that would otherwise be silently filled with defaults.

Borrow attention to the human’s actual description, explicit assumptions and competing approaches. Use project evidence to avoid asking settled questions. A short change can need a concise statement of direction rather than a full project dossier; communicate the consequential calls so the person can correct them.

## Mismatches and limits

The design-document approval gate and next-skill sequence are this workflow’s operational policy. They must not be imported automatically into a task where the user already authorized implementation or delegated choices. Menus can steer answers, but open questions can also demand too much abstraction; adapt to the person. No interview, companion server or downstream plan was executed in this inspection.

# SwiftUI expert: native layout and state review

## When to use

Choose this when a SwiftUI design must become a resilient native interface, or when a view breaks during resizing, navigation or changing text. It helps connect a proposed design to state ownership and platform layout behavior; it does not supply a brand or research the audience.

## What to inspect

Read the router and the topic-specific reference before applying a change. The inspected layout reference emphasizes the size offered to the view, local environment values, safe-area ownership and preservation of identity. Match its API advice to the project deployment target and SDK; the pinned source includes emerging platform-version claims that this curation did not independently verify.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the distinction between a decision about available space and a decision about device capability. Check how a card behaves in a sheet, a split window and a full screen, rather than assuming a device-sized frame. Preserve navigation and reading state through layout changes. The entrypoint avoids imposing an architecture such as MVVM and restricts Liquid Glass adoption to explicit requests.

## Mismatches and limits

This is a large implementation knowledge router, not evidence that a resulting app is usable or visually successful. Profiling and recording paths can invoke scripts and processes; selection is not authorization to run them. Do not mechanically turn every fixed dimension into a percentage or every suggestion into a performance requirement. Inspect relevant references and actual runtime behavior before claiming acceptance.

## Related resource roles

- [system-apple-hig](system-apple-hig.md): Connect the implementation method to native interaction guidance and the actual supported system version.

# UI/UX Pro Max: contextual local design search

## When to use

Select this when the task needs a catalog-style source of design options or stack-specific implementation guidance. It is especially relevant to the library’s discovery problem because it distinguishes product-wide direction, targeted concerns and known-stack searches.

## What to inspect

Read the Query Contract before the example commands. Inspect the source’s returned domain/identity checks, contextual retry and no-verified-match behavior. Review persistence and existing master/override rules separately from searching; they are different operations with different effects.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow searching by one dominant intent and a useful constraint, detecting the actual stack, and checking returned applicability before using it. For a form correction, search the semantic outcome first, then obtain implementation detail for the project’s stack. Preserve already accepted design decisions when saving or updating a system.

## Mismatches and limits

The data totals and style names describe the package, not measured recommendation quality. Generalized numeric UX rules still need the applicable standard and context. The inspected instruction describes a Python search script; its retrieval, data quality and persistence were not executed or audited here. # Vercel React best practices

## When to use

Select this after React or Next.js is actually part of the project and the design has implementation consequences for loading, responsiveness or repeated rendering. It is useful for a data-heavy interface whose layout is coherent but whose work arrives late or blocks interaction.

## What to inspect

Start with the relevant priority category, then read the individual rule and its context. A short slogan about imports or caching is not enough. Inspect the project’s framework/version and existing data lifecycle before transferring an example.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow prioritization by the actual bottleneck and examples that explain the mechanism. Check independent requests, component boundaries, serialization, loading state and resource cost. Tie a proposed optimization to an observable user path and measure what changes. A dashboard that fetches unrelated panels sequentially raises a different question from an expensive repeated table render.

## Mismatches and limits

It does not choose the product flow, brand voice or visual hierarchy. Listed impact levels are author-maintained priorities, not measurements for this application. React-specific recipes should not migrate an unrelated stack or replace working code without benefit. Some detailed rules include alternatives that a blanket ban would erase. Instructions were read, not benchmarked here.

# Vercel Web Interface Guidelines review

Select this for a bounded review of existing web-interface code when the immediate need is actionable findings rather than a new visual world. It complements a design direction by checking implementation details across semantics, content, layout robustness and interaction.

## What to inspect

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow a concise evidence-to-fix report: locate a concrete element or declaration, explain its consequence, and propose a scoped repair. Apply the relevant checks to the changed surface. For a settings form, this can expose a missing control name or misleading loading label while retaining the established brand and layout.

## Mismatches and limits

The procedure is a review mechanism, not a source of distinctive art direction. Its instruction to fetch and obey every remote rule must yield to task scope and higher-priority constraints. # Focus and motion: preserve control across interaction changes

## When to use

Use when designing animated navigation, expanding content, dialogs, drag feedback or focus treatments that accompany state changes.

## What to inspect

Compare AA Focus Visible with AAA Focus Appearance rather than merging them. For motion, distinguish automatically moving content from nonessential interaction-triggered animation and preserve essential-motion exceptions. Read the criterion's actual scope before choosing a technique.

## What to borrow and adapt

Keep the current interaction point perceivable, preserve meaningful focus after changes, and offer an appropriate reduced-motion experience without losing state or functionality. A reduced transition should still communicate completion and keep controls available.

For a row expansion, the selected object and newly exposed content should remain understandable with less movement. A decorative entrance sequence should not hide essential content indefinitely when animation is disabled or interrupted.

## Mismatches and limits

The two-pixel-perimeter equivalent is an area condition, not one mandatory outline style. AAA criteria are not automatically AA requirements, although a project may choose stronger behavior. Disabling all animations can break poorly coupled state callbacks; verify the resulting operation. This card does not certify accessible motion or replace platform/user research.

# Accessible text: contrast, overrides and reflow

## When to use

Use when a visual direction includes small or faint text, fixed-size cards, long translated labels, dense tables, or typography that must survive zoom and reader overrides.

## What to inspect

Read the relevant normative criteria and explanatory exceptions. Text Spacing defines tolerance for user overrides, not compulsory authored spacing. Reflow distinguishes vertical-scrolling width from horizontal-scrolling height and preserves essential two-dimensional content exceptions.

## What to borrow and adapt

Treat typography, layout and state as a connected system. Check actual foreground/background pairs, meaningful text roles, content-driven dimensions and enlarged text. Preserve access to labels, errors, controls and comparison information when content wraps.

For a dense table, assess cells and surrounding controls rather than automatically converting every row into a card. For an expressive heading, preserve its character while testing real long text and fallback rendering.

## Mismatches and limits

Meeting a nominal color ratio does not establish comfortable reading, and an exception for a logo or inactive element does not excuse unrelated text. Do not require the override test values as default CSS or infer complete accessibility from a screenshot. This is a scoped standard resource, not a palette, universal font-size rule or evidence of product conformance.

# WCAG conformance scope

## When to use

Use when a design brief includes an accessibility target, a review needs clear acceptance criteria, or a team is about to describe an interface as compliant. Start here before extracting a few convenient color or focus rules.

## What to inspect

Read the normative criterion and its level, then the conformance requirements concerning complete pages, complete processes, accessibility-supported technologies and non-interference. Level AA includes all Level A and AA criteria, or the specified conforming-alternate-version route. Full-page scope includes automatically presented responsive variations; each must conform or have the required conforming alternate. Use Understanding documents for explanation while preserving their distinction from the standard.

## What to borrow and adapt

Create a scoped requirement/evidence map for the actual journey. A booking flow can span choice, correction, confirmation and cancellation; testing only its opening card does not establish the process. State which version, level, pages, responsive variations, states and technologies were assessed and what remains unobserved.

Apply checks relevant to the chosen target without turning an example technique into the only permitted implementation. Preserve the person's brand and task goals while finding a conforming design.

## Mismatches and limits

WCAG conformance is not a universal score for usability, attractiveness or every disability-related need. A validator output or screenshot does not establish complete-process conformance. This card is not legal advice, a certification or evidence that any cataloged product conforms. A current project may have additional platform, contractual or user requirements.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

## When to use

Use when the experience belongs on an Apple platform and platform behavior matters to recognition, input or system integration. Ask which platforms, window sizes, assistive technologies and system surfaces are actually in scope.

## What to inspect

Use the platform and topic navigation to find the relevant guidance, then inspect a specific pattern and its implementation documentation. This review read the onboarding body and navigation in native Chrome. It did not inspect every foundation, component or platform-specific chapter.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow platform-aware questions before choosing a layout: what does the operating system already teach, which system control should carry an action, and where can learning occur in context? For a small creative utility, examine whether direct manipulation with lightweight help would teach better than a prerequisite presentation. Use the companion onboarding card as a focused starting point.

## Mismatches and limits

HIG is guidance for Apple ecosystems, not a complete web design system or an implementation library. A native-looking control does not prove native behavior. Cross-platform products may require shared product concepts with different platform presentations. The source was readable in native Chrome after the text extractor returned a JavaScript shell; no native application was launched and no full visual identity was evaluated.

# Atlassian Design System

## When to use

Use when comparing systems for collaborative product UI or establishing typography roles in an existing application. Ask whether the work is a brand campaign, a product screen, or both, and what font licensing and platform fallback constraints already exist.

## What to inspect

Read the typography chapter’s separation of brand and product fonts, role tokens and fallback treatment. The source discusses Charlie Sans for brand contexts and Atlassian Sans/Mono for product work. Inspect the foundation and component routes for the specific surface; the homepage alone is not an adoption guide.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the decision structure rather than the font names. For a planning application, define reading, heading, code and metadata roles, connect them to tokens, and test realistic content lengths. Keep marketing expression and dense working screens related through identity without requiring identical typographic treatment. Resolve hierarchy and scanning with representative tasks before choosing weights.

## Mismatches and limits

This source is a useful counterexample to universal prohibitions on bold headings or particular font categories: coherent systems make contextual decisions. It is not permission to redistribute Atlassian’s fonts or copy its brand. No typography screenshots were visually inspected and no package was executed. Accessibility requires rendered size, contrast, zoom, language and content checks in the resulting product.

# Carbon Design System

## When to use

Use as a candidate when teams need coherent conventions for a substantial operational product. Ask about operator expertise, data volume, repetition, accessibility support and the cost of adopting an existing component family.

## What to inspect

Start at components and patterns for the real job, then check implementation and version. The inspected homepage exposes foundations, data visualization and related building blocks; it also discusses future v12 work. An announcement about future visuals does not identify the behavior of the currently installed library.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the method of connecting tokens, interaction guidance and task patterns. For an inventory console, compare the data-table guidance with empty states before choosing density and actions. Write a local mapping from supported user tasks to selected components, and use that mapping to avoid inventing slightly different controls on every screen.

## Mismatches and limits

Carbon carries IBM product and brand assumptions. A public cultural publication or casual mobile game may need a different reference family. The homepage establishes ecosystem scope, not measured usability, complete accessibility conformance or a rendered visual match. Read the specific component implementation and test its composed behavior. The companion table and empty-state cards provide narrower entry points.

# Fluent 2

## When to use

Use when a productivity product needs to align with Microsoft ecosystem conventions or when comparing systems with web and native implementation routes. Ask which platform library the project actually uses and what consistency must mean across those platforms.

## What to inspect

Inspect the platform route before selecting a component. The homepage separates web, iOS, Android and Windows resources and connects design and development tooling. Read the individual component guidance, status and implementation instead of assuming a single API spans every platform.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the practice of carrying a product’s intent across platform-specific components. For an internal approval tool, define the decision, required information and recovery path first, then choose the supported dialog or page pattern for each client. Document which tokens and interaction expectations remain shared and which follow the host platform.

## Mismatches and limits

Fluent’s ecosystem fit can be valuable without making its house style universally appropriate. A branded editorial experience or a specialist creative canvas may need different references. Homepage inspection did not verify visual assets, library runtime behavior or accessibility across platforms. The companion dialog card examines one web React guideline; it does not establish that other implementations have identical dismissal and focus behavior.

# Pinterest Gestalt: investigation candidate

## When to use

Keep this as a candidate when broadening a shortlist beyond enterprise and government systems toward a consumer-product organization. It is a place to investigate, not yet a recommendation for a specific Pinterest-like design or behavior.

## What to inspect

The public landing describes a shared Pinterest design language and links to foundations, components and getting started. The deeper overview routes did not expose enough substantive guidance in this research pass. Before promotion, inspect actual decision guidance, supported implementations, component states and a representative screen through an approved public surface.

## What to borrow and adapt

The transferable next step is a focused comparison question: does the current system offer guidance relevant to the user’s actual discovery, saving or organization task? Ask the user which of those tasks and what expressive direction matter, then inspect relevant material. Record observed evidence rather than inferring a visual style from Pinterest’s reputation.

## Mismatches and limits

No source-supported claim about component quality, visual character, motion or accessibility is made. Only the landing and route availability were examined; no component, native product or flow was tested. This explicit candidate preserves the research gap so an agent will not quietly substitute name recognition for evidence. Compare curated systems while deeper access remains unresolved.

# GOV.UK Design System

## When to use

Start here when a person must complete an occasional, consequential service transaction and needs understandable questions, progress and correction. It is especially relevant when the agent needs a coherent family of patterns rather than a single fashionable component.

## What to inspect

Use the system's styles/components/patterns distinction to locate the right level of guidance. Read the pattern for the actual user job, then its component and accessibility notes. The homepage is a route into maintainer guidance, not sufficient implementation instruction by itself.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the connection between content, semantic components and an end-to-end task. For a local membership application, for example, use a concise question protocol and a review/correction route while adapting vocabulary, eligibility and support to the community. Preserve the chosen project's own identity; a GOV.UK-looking page would imply an authority that an unrelated product may not possess.

## Mismatches and limits

This is a government-service system with its own brand, conventions and institutional requirements. It does not decide the best information density for expert operators, an expressive publication's atmosphere, or a game's interaction model. Homepage announcements establish documentation state, not a passing accessibility audit of any downstream implementation. No screen was visually inspected for this card.

# GitHub Primer

## When to use

Use when studying a developer-oriented product system or separating an organization’s application and marketing references. Ask what task belongs in a working product and what belongs in a brand or promotional surface.

## What to inspect

Inspect the Product UI and Brand UI routes before reading components. Then check component implementation availability and the linked guidelines. The inspected action-menu route connects an overlay and action list; its existence does not establish that any arbitrary menu composition is suitable.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the surface distinction and a common vocabulary of roles. For a deployment tool, choose operational components for frequent commands and status reading, while allowing the launch page its own composition within the broader identity. Keep icon, token and accessibility decisions consistent across the selected product family. The companion action-menu card supplies a more specific decision about commands versus input.

## Mismatches and limits

GitHub’s interaction and visual conventions are not neutral defaults for every audience. A novice public service or expressive publication may need different references. No rendered Primer screen or React/Rails implementation was tested here. Product and Brand routes are related resources, not independent validation of one another. Package readiness, exact API support and downstream accessibility must be checked for the project’s version.

# Radix Primitives

## When to use

Use when the team needs reusable behavior under a custom visual identity and has the capacity to compose and test a product UI. Ask who owns styling, content, state, focus and integration across primitive boundaries.

## What to inspect

Read the introduction’s unstyled approach, composition and controlled-state model, then the exact primitive API. Inspect how a trigger, portal, content, labels and state callbacks cooperate. The companion dialog card includes one narrow demo interaction, which is stronger evidence than the introduction’s general capability claims.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow a separation between component behavior and visual tokens. For a bespoke research tool, use a primitive for a familiar interaction while defining clear names, task-specific actions and a coherent type/spacing system locally. Record how custom wrappers preserve semantics and ref/focus behavior. Choose the smallest abstraction that the project can maintain.

## Mismatches and limits

Primitives do not provide an information architecture, screen flow, brand or finished accessibility result. Styling and composition can undermine their intended behavior. The vendor’s accessibility goals are source claims rather than an independent audit. A team wanting ready-composed application pages should compare a fuller system. This card does not recommend introducing React or replacing an adequate native HTML control merely to use a primitive.

## When to use

The inspected accordion wrapper exposes several guidance sections, but its embedded usage material was only partially readable through this research tool.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow an investigation plan: map a creative task to controls, inspect states and behaviors, and compare the resulting composition with the local product’s input and content needs. For a media inspector, examine whether disclosure and grouping help the real adjustment task; do not infer that the Adobe association alone makes a pattern suitable. Use current implementation docs to resolve the question.

## Mismatches and limits

This card is curated as an ecosystem-routing reference, not a component recommendation or a visual match. An older action-group URL returned 404 and no action-group guidance is represented here. # U.S. Web Design System

## When to use

Use when a U.S. public-service project needs a coherent reference, or when studying accessible service patterns with explicit content and institutional context. Ask which service standards apply and whether adopting the system is a requirement or a comparison option.

## What to inspect

Navigate among principles, patterns, components and the maturity model instead of starting with a template screenshot. Check the current package and documentation version. The user-profile family illustrates how institutional policy can change field guidance; it should not be treated as a timeless inventory of data every product must collect.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the connection between a user job, content, implementation guidance and incremental adoption. For a local benefits service, map language access, form completion and recovery before selecting components. The language-pattern family is especially useful for distinguishing a fully translated site from a site with only selected translated materials.

## Mismatches and limits

USWDS carries federal context and policy obligations. Adapt jurisdiction, language, identity and information requirements rather than copying official banners or collecting unnecessary profile data. Homepage and pattern-source inspection did not test a deployed service, a responsive template or assistive technology. The observed v3.14.0 label is a snapshot; verify the installed version and current standards before implementation.

Borrow the idea of turning a reference into role-based, implementation-relevant notes. Separate the visual role from exact values and identify the particular quality the human wants. # axe-core: state-scoped accessibility checks

## When to use

Select axe-core as one verification instrument when an implemented web interface needs repeatable checks for automatically detectable accessibility problems. It fits an existing browser-testing workflow and can target a changed component or state instead of treating the whole application as one static screenshot.

## What to inspect

Read the API Notes and `axe.run` context/options/results contract. The Playwright guide gives a concrete sequence that opens a menu, waits for its visible state and scans that region. Check current integration versions before adding tooling to the project.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow state-scoped testing: reach the relevant state first, run the appropriate checks, retain the result categories and inspect the referenced elements. Apply this to an error summary, expanded menu, open dialog or dynamically filtered result. Choose rules and exclusions according to the claim being made, documenting meaningful exclusions rather than suppressing unexplained failures.

Keep a route for incomplete results needing human review. Complement the scan with keyboard, focus, content and intended-user checks; tool output is one evidence source.

## Mismatches and limits

The API checks rendered content, so a clean initial-page scan does not cover hidden menus or future errors. Automated checks cannot establish all WCAG requirements, reader comprehension or task usability. No scan ran during this curation pass. Selecting this card does not authorize an installation, accessing a prohibited page, or treating an unavailable browser as permission to try another route.

## Related resource roles

- [standard-wcag-conformance](standard-wcag-conformance.md): An automated scan cannot by itself establish complete-process conformance.
- [principle-native-semantics](principle-native-semantics.md): Control semantics and keyboard behavior complement automatically detectable findings.

# Chrome DevTools: inspect applied CSS rather than infer tokens

## When to use

Select DevTools CSS inspection when an authorized rendered page must be understood at the level of applied declarations or layout geometry. It helps distinguish exact implementation observations from visual estimates while investigating a mismatch or reconstructing limited design guidance.

## What to inspect

Read the applied-style, pseudostate and box-model examples. Inspect the actual element and state in the intended viewport, with its cascade and relevant stylesheet. A declared custom property is not necessarily the value currently used by the element.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow evidence from the rendered consumer: which rule wins, what changes under a state, and which dimensions derive from content or constraints. Connect repeated values to their actual owners before calling them a shared token system. A locally toggled declaration can test a small hypothesis; preserve its provisional status and implement the real fix in source only when requested.

## Mismatches and limits

One element’s computed value does not establish a site-wide intention, reusable scale or accessibility outcome. Browser overrides can mask source defects and disappear on reload. Access to a browser inspection tool does not authorize reading unrelated private tabs or bypassing URL policy. This card inspected the official tutorial only; no page, computed style or visual was examined during this curation.

# Excalidraw: editable low-fidelity relationship sketches

## When to use

Select Excalidraw when an editable rough arrangement, relationship diagram or low-fidelity flow would help the person react to an idea. It can keep discussion focused on structure and alternatives before fine typography or component styling dominates the conversation.

## What to inspect

Read the distinction between the editor package and hosted application, export options and the SDK FAQ. The package does not automatically provide the hosted service’s collaboration behavior. Check what workspace and sharing authority the task actually provides.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow a deliberately small sketch: actors, important content groups, primary actions and transitions with labels explaining their role. Compare two structures using the same real content. A hand-drawn appearance can signal provisionality, but explicitly state what is and is not decided; visual roughness alone does not guarantee open critique.

## Mismatches and limits

A diagram’s attractiveness does not establish a good flow, and an exported image does not preserve an interactive application. Hosted collaboration, share links and integrations can have external effects. Selection is not permission to create a shared room or publish a drawing. Source documentation was inspected; no canvas, export, collaboration session or embedded implementation was executed.

# Lighthouse: scoped page-quality diagnostics

## When to use

Select Lighthouse when a working web page needs repeatable diagnostics of loading or automatically checkable quality properties. It can help investigate why an otherwise coherent design feels slow or exposes avoidable technical problems.

## What to inspect

Read the workflow options and audit references rather than treating the aggregate score as the result. Choose an authorized local, authenticated or public-page route appropriate to the task. Check the tool/browser version and test conditions before comparing reports.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow using a failed diagnostic as a question with a traceable element or mechanism. Connect the result to the intended user path: a shifted action, delayed content, missing name or blocking script has a specific consequence. Preserve the report configuration so a later comparison measures the same conditions. Keep local reports local unless sharing is requested.

## Mismatches and limits

A good score does not establish task completion, accessibility conformance, comprehension or visual relevance. A single page-load run also omits many later states. The official documentation includes optional hosted analysis and report-sharing operations; selecting this resource does not authorize sending a private URL or report to them. No audit, installation, report upload or real page test was performed during curation.

# Mobbin: screen and flow discovery with access limits

## When to use

Select Mobbin as a discovery route when the local library lacks relevant shipped app or site references. It can point a researcher toward consumer/mobile contexts that are underrepresented in public design-system documentation.

## What to inspect

Inspect the available search categories and the actual authorized example, screen sequence, platform and date. The public product page was read here; full subscription content, search results and member-only flow bodies were not accessed. Verify access before proposing a task that depends on them.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the practice of searching by a concrete job or interaction rather than a fashionable style label. Compare neighboring products and preserve the exact state or sequence being used. A selected example can suggest what to inspect in the original product, while the human explains which qualities fit their own audience and intent.

## Mismatches and limits

The public marketing page and its collection claims do not establish the contents or quality of every reference. No screenshots were visually inspected in this card, and no recorded flow was tested. Do not assert that an unavailable example matches the brief, infer present behavior from an old capture, bypass paid access, or redistribute product screenshots. This is a curated discovery-tool entry with partial access, not a vetted recommendation for particular unseen screens.

## Related resource roles

- [pattern-apple-onboarding](pattern-apple-onboarding.md): Combine a research directory with platform guidance; only inspected accessible screens can support specific visual/flow claims.

# Penpot: explicit prototype boards, triggers and flows

## When to use

Select Penpot when the person needs an editable visual prototype to discuss screen relationships, navigation or alternate starting points before committing to production behavior. It can support a collaborative artifact where rearranging and comparing screens is easier than discussing abstract style labels.

## What to inspect

Read board connections, triggers/actions and flows in the current guide. Identify the task’s actual entry point and relevant error/recovery branches before wiring screens. Check whether an overlay, previous-screen action or separate flow reflects the intended model.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow explicit representation of an interaction: origin, trigger, action and destination. Include meaningful alternate paths rather than only a presentation tour. A first-time signup and an existing member’s return can have distinct start points while sharing components and brand. Keep the prototype’s fidelity and missing behavior clear to the human reviewer.

## Mismatches and limits

A connected board can mimic navigation without implementing validation, persistence, permissions or responsive behavior. A prototype is therefore not proof of a working service. Sharing links, uploading assets, creating teams or installing/self-hosting the software are separate actions. The public guide was read, but no Penpot file, prototype interaction or account was opened in this curation.

# Playwright: interaction and visual comparison evidence

## When to use

Select Playwright when the task needs repeatable evidence that an implemented interaction reaches the expected state or a known design changed unexpectedly. It is a verification capability match, not a source of brand or flow design.

## What to inspect

Read the action/assertion guidance relevant to the flow, the accessibility example’s state setup, and the screenshot-environment warnings. Confirm the repository’s existing framework and browser setup before introducing another test path. A screenshot baseline is a versioned artifact whose origin matters.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow observable sequences: select, submit, encounter an error, correct, confirm and reset. Assert the meaningful state at each consequential transition. Reach hidden content before scanning it. Use screenshots to compare composition under controlled rendering conditions, then inspect whether a detected difference is expected. Separate automation, manual accessibility review and intended-user testing.

## Mismatches and limits

A passing pixel comparison can preserve a bad design; a failing one can reflect fonts, operating system or hardware rather than a product regression. Automated accessibility scans catch only part of the problem. Tool access must be explicitly permitted; a browser denial is not permission to retry by another route. No package, browser or test was installed/executed for this card.

# Storybook: component state catalog and interaction fixtures

## When to use

Select Storybook when a component family needs an inspectable state vocabulary, shared review surface or repeatable interaction fixture. It is useful after a design direction exists and the team needs to see whether its controls work across meaningful content and states.

## What to inspect

Read how a story defines initial arguments/context and how an interaction test acts on that state. Inspect representative local stories instead of assuming a component gallery covers the real product. Match the documentation version to the project’s installed version.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow making selected, disabled, loading, error, empty and long-content cases explicit where the component supports them. Use a compact set of meaningful variants rather than an exhaustive visual matrix with no tasks. A booking control’s error recovery or a table’s empty-filter state can become a reviewable fixture with a clear expected transition.

## Mismatches and limits

Component isolation can hide routing, authentication, data ownership and page-level layout problems. A polished gallery is not an end-to-end flow or proof of design quality. Mock data and providers must represent the relevant conditions honestly. Publishing stories or adding hosted visual-testing services are separate actions. Documentation was inspected; no Storybook build, play function or visual suite ran.

# Are.na: a text-led invitation to a knowledge community

## When to use

Use as a counterexample to assuming that a welcoming community needs cartoon artwork, colorful benefit tiles or a large decorative headline. It suits investigation of content-led identity and a distinctive conceptual vocabulary.

## What to inspect

Inspect the opening definition, short community explanation, small action pair and transition into the product model. The screenshot covers the public introduction; partially loaded product-preview areas are not evidence of the application's working interface.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the decision to explain a community through its activity and material. For a reading or research club, specific examples of what people collect or connect can express character more precisely than generic friendliness.

Adapt the language to newcomers. A deliberately unusual definition can invite curiosity but can also hide what someone should do next. Test comprehension instead of importing the tone wholesale. Compare this text-led direction with an illustrated invitation when helping the person articulate the intended atmosphere.

## Mismatches and limits

No account, collection or collaborative action was exercised. The observed dark theme is one presentation, not a universal requirement. The screenshot does not verify claims about recommendations, membership or community outcomes. Strong editorial identity can be a poor fit for urgent transactional work where people need a direct answer.

# Brilliant: make the learning material visible

## When to use

Use when the subject matter can demonstrate the product more meaningfully than stock photos or generic benefits. It is a reference for making a learning proposition concrete through examples of the actual material.

## What to inspect

Inspect the current hero, differentiated audience actions and mathematical panels. The viewed page emphasizes tutoring and visible problem representations; do not substitute a remembered older version of the brand. No problem was solved or lesson opened.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow subject-specific visual evidence: show the kind of question, object or transformation people will work with. For a creative tool, that could be a real editing example; for a community workshop, an actual activity or artifact. Keep examples intelligible at the displayed scale.

Adapt the composition to the information's structure. A fan of panels can imply range but may become decorative if every panel is unreadable. Ask which material should be understood immediately and which can serve as atmosphere.

## Mismatches and limits

The screenshot does not verify tutoring quality, learning outcomes, interaction, device behavior or audience suitability. Mathematical imagery must remain correct if adapted; invented equations are not harmless filler. The brand's serif choice and panel arrangement are not universal requirements for education.

# Finch: a companion world around a simple invitation

## When to use

Use to explore whether a friendly companion or small illustrated world fits a consumer product. It can help a person articulate warmth, reassurance and attachment more concretely than asking whether they want a “friendly” design.

## What to inspect

Inspect both the upper invitation and the landscape below it: the bird icon, large outlined type, sky/ground separation, two companion characters and store badges. The observed surface is the marketing page; no app account or self-care task was opened.

## What to borrow and adapt

Borrow the alignment between the product metaphor and visual world. Character, setting and invitation speak together; they are not isolated decorative stickers. An original companion may fit a habit or community project if the owner wants that relationship. Ask which qualities matter—gentleness, companionship, customization or a miniature world—and adapt the mechanism accordingly.

Keep the next action clear and use actual product content. The inspected page is a useful contrast to Duolingo's white-space-and-collage composition, despite both using bird characters.

## Mismatches and limits

The screenshot does not establish therapeutic efficacy, habit outcomes, accessibility or app usability. Ratings displayed by the page were not independently verified and should not be copied as evidence. Do not import emotional attachment mechanics into consequential professional workflows by default. Character artwork and brand assets are not licensed by this card.
